Q: NRF52: How to erase a protected firmware program (knowing the protected password) A:

Using OpenOCD 0.11.0 (binaries available from https://github.com/xpack-dev-tools/openocd-xpack/releases/tag/v0.11.0-1/ )

The following commands will remove the chip protection and reprogram the chip (with the lp.hex program)

bin\openocd -f interface/cmsis-dap.cfg -f target/nrf52.cfg -c "telnet_port pipe;tcl_port disabled;gdb_port disabled;log_output 
reset init
nrf52_recover
flash write_image s132_nrf52_2.0.1_softdevice.hex
flash write_image lp.hex
reset

This works for all versions fo the chips including the later versions (build Gxx and later) which automatically re-apply chip protection on reset.

For those of you using Arduino, my Very Low Power BLE <20uA project automates this process in the Arduino sketch upload.

Also see https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/nordic/nordic-blog/b/blog/posts/working-with-the-nrf52-series-improved-approtect

Q: Run an async function weekly at a specific time A:

function=demo_fx() calls the function and passes the return value, which is None. Then schedule does function(*args), so you'd get TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable. Pass the function itself.

function=demo_fx

Your condition day.capitalize() not in days or day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow" is always true, since a day can't be both in the dict and equal to "Tomorrow". Every call returns the error string, and asyncio.sleep then gets a str. You want and.

if (day.capitalize() not in days and day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow") or hour < 0 or hour > 23:

If today is Sunday and it's already past the target hour, % 7 gives 0, so you compute a delay in the past and asyncio.sleep returns immediately. Check for a negative delta and add a week.

if delta.total_seconds() < 0:
    full_datetime += timedelta(days=7)

Q: Cannot clone nRF52840 to reproduce low deep sleep current A:

The winning command is:

nrfjprog.exe  --readcode --readuicr --readram [filename.hex]

Apparently, the --readram was the winning flag, as without it the sketch simply doesn't run at the same current consumption for whatever reason. But now, I can reproducibly image and transfer identical firmware, which was what I was after.

Q: Codex CLI Update Error - missing OSArchitecture property A:

Use PowerShell 7 (Recommended)

The most reliable way to fix this and prevent future script compatibility issues with CLI tools is to use the modern version of PowerShell.

  • Open your current terminal and install it via the Windows Package Manager by typing: winget install --id Microsoft.Powershell --source winget

  • Once installed, open this new terminal (search your Start menu for PowerShell 7 or simply type pwsh in your current terminal to switch over).

  • Run your codex command again. The update script should now successfully detect your system architecture and complete the update.
    OR

    Manual Update Bypass

    If you prefer not to install a new version of PowerShell, you can bypass the auto-updater entirely.

    • Set an environment variable to temporarily disable the auto-updater so you can continue using your current version: $env:CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1

    • Alternatively, visit the official Codex CLI repository or website to download the latest Windows binary directly.

    • Replace the old codex.exe executable inside your installation path with the newly downloaded version.
